investment.label: Planned 2026 investment in U.S. facilities
investment.definition: Planned 2026 investment at a U.S. site as itemised in GE Aerospace's March 9, 2026 release (part of 'another $1 billion' for 'sites across more than 30 communities in 17 states'). Plans, not actual spend. A state row is used only where the release's itemised site is the only site GE Aerospace's investment map shows in that state; other itemised sites are recorded as sites.

notes: Investment is the 2026 plan from GE Aerospace's March 9, 2026 release (newer than the March 2024 and March 2025 plans): another $1 billion for U.S. sites 'across more than 30 communities in 17 states', of which the release itemises Cincinnati, OH ($115M), Lynn, MA ($40M+), Madisonville, KY ($10M), Durham, NC ($20M) and Lafayette, IN ($7M), plus $200M for LEAP durability kits and more than $100M for suppliers (no site or state given). GE Aerospace's interactive investment map (geaerospace.com/manufacturing) shows site amounts only in page code, so it was used only to check which states have more than one site: Massachusetts shows one, so Lynn is a state row (MA, '$40+', marked plus); Kentucky, North Carolina, Indiana and Ohio show several, so those amounts are recorded as sites, not state values, and nothing was summed. The 2024 plan's Alabama and North Carolina state rows and its 'about $100 million at international sites in North America, Europe and India' region row were removed: the 2026 release itemises no Alabama or international amount and gives no North Carolina total. The Auburn, Asheville, West Jefferson and Wilmington sites keep their March 12, 2024 release descriptions (2024 plan amounts). 10-K (FY2025): ~57,000 employees, ~30,000 in the U.S. (US country row); manufacturing and service operations at 70 facilities in 23 states and Puerto Rico and 62 facilities in 23 other countries, with no breakdown by state or country.
